sourceFile: PDF ("Cycle of Prayer | September 6, 2026 – August 31, 2027") supplied directly by Josh, since the diocese's own hosted Flipsnack flipbook (https://www.flipsnack.com/diodel/ecd-cycle-of-prayer/full-view.html) could not be fetched from this session's sandbox.
notes: Source is a single PDF ("THE EPISCOPAL CHURCH IN DELAWARE / Cycle of Prayer | September 6, 2026 – August 31, 2027", revised September 6, 2026) supplied directly by Josh after Flipsnack's own hosted version of this cycle (https://www.flipsnack.com/diodel/ecd-cycle-of-prayer/full-view.html) proved unfetchable from this session's sandbox -- individual flipbook page images returned HTTP 403 even by direct URL, and a headless-browser render hit the same TLS/cert block this project has already documented for other external asset CDNs (see AUDIT_GOVERNANCE_LEDGER.md).

This single source document spans two calendar years (Sept 6, 2026 – Aug 31, 2027, 52 weekly entries total). Per this schema's own 'one file per diocese per year' rule, it is split into two files here: this one (episcopal-delaware-2026.json, the 17 entries from Sept 6 through Dec 27, 2026) and a companion episcopal-delaware-2027.json (the remaining 35 entries, Jan 3 through Aug 29, 2027) -- both transcribed from the identical source PDF. This is a deliberate split for app resolvability (the app's own year-keyed lookup would never find the 2027 dates if they stayed in a 2026-dated file), not a gap or omission in either direction.

Every parish subject's clergy/warden line (e.g. 'The Rev. Patrick T. Burke, Rector') is recorded in that subject's own `note` field, per the existing precedent in episcopal-great-lakes-2026.json and this batch's own episcopal-indianapolis-2026.json/episcopal-kansas-2026.json -- the schema has no dedicated clergy field, and `note` is the correct place for a per-subject disclosure.

December 13, 2026 names two congregations together ("All Saints' Church, Rehoboth Beach, and St. George's Chapel, Harbeson") sharing one clergy team -- transcribed as two separate `parish` subjects (one per named congregation, each carrying the identical shared-clergy `note`), not folded into one subject, since these are two distinct, currently-existing congregations rather than one congregation under alternate/historical names (contrast with Chicago's 'Trinity (formerly St. Ann...)' merger precedent, which genuinely was one congregation).

October 11, 2026 (2026 file) and January 24, 2027 (2027 file) each name multiple distinct diocesan-wide items in one sentence -- split into separate `category` subjects, matching this batch's own Kansas precedent for the same pattern.

February 14, 2027: "St. Anne's School, Middletown" is recorded as `category` (an institution, not a congregation) rather than `parish`, distinguishing it from "St. Andrew's School Chapel, Middletown" (Jan 31, 2027) which explicitly names a chapel and is recorded as `parish`, consistent with this corpus's existing 'Episcopal City Mission' precedent (a schema-defined `parish` type covers 'a parish, mission, or cathedral', not a school in its own right).

June 13, 2027: "Camp Arrowhead and Memorial House" is transcribed as one `category` subject as printed, not split -- treated as a single camp/retreat-center complex rather than two separate named entities, since the source gives no indication they are administratively distinct the way, e.g., the Jan 24 Daughters of the King / Anamchara Fellowship pairing does.

Apostrophes preserved as printed in the source (a straight ' in most names, one curly ’ in "O’Connor"), following this corpus's per-file convention of matching the specific source document rather than normalizing corpus-wide.
This file covers the second (2027) portion of the source's Sept 2026 – Aug 2027 cycle -- see episcopal-delaware-2026.json for the Sept–Dec 2026 portion transcribed from the same document.
